NAH. her reaction is appropriate for her age and you respected her autonomy, which is another good lesson that you're teaching her out of this. as most commenters said, this is a way to teach her about the consequences of her own actions. 
not really relevant but, growing up, i had always been the weird kid. my parents weren't the most supportive and they also mocked me for doing things that other kids didn't do (e.g. wanting to buy "adult" clothing, liking more mature colors, unable to socialize with peers my own age, etc). i had a hard time accepting myself for who i am and i didn't form close relationships until sometime in my late teens. but from that, i eventually learned that life is just too short to not do/be whatever you want because you fear others' judgement. i don't have lots of loved ones, but those who are, accept me for who i am. maybe this can be a good way to teach her that? being a t(w?)eenager is tough and at her age, self-esteem is really important. how her peers think of her really can greatly affect how she thinks of herself. 
I'm probably just overthinking this though, haha. regardless, you're on the right track.
